meta.unit_of_analysis: snapshots of one training run are correlated; run-level summaries are given wherever a spread is quoted (36 add/grok runs, 9 lin runs; the 35 add/memo models are 35 separate runs)

A1.definition: t0_mean = mean over x != 0 of T_x(0); law = pc_law(eps, q, 2) at the model's realised eps; naive = (1-eps)^2; dev = measured - prediction; overdisp = sd over x != 0 of T_x(0) (ddof 1) divided by sqrt(P(1-P)/|G|) with P = t0_mean
A1.identity: mean_{x != 0} T_x(0) = (|G| S - 1)/(|G| - 1), S = sum_v pi_v^2 the collision probability of the error-value histogram (pi_0 = 1 - eps): the MEAN per-vote correctness depends only on the histogram of error values, not on where the errors are.  Hence dev_law = value_conc - fs_term with value_conc = sum_{v != 0} pi_v^2 - eps^2/(q-1) >= 0 and fs_term = (1 - S)/(|G| - 1).
A1.overdispersion_note: The binomial value sqrt(P(1-P)/|G|) is NOT a calibrated reference: for matched i.i.d. fields the ratio is below 1 (the |G| terms of N_0(x) share one fixed error set and are negatively dependent; at small eps the ratio tends to sqrt(2 eps)).  The calibrated statistic is overdisp_over_matched_iid = overdisp(model) / median overdisp of its 20 matched i.i.d. fields.

A2.definition: maxwrong = max over x != 0, h != 0 of T_x(h).  coh_ratio_iid = maxwrong / median of the same statistic over 20 matched i.i.d. fields PER MODEL (same group, exactly the same number of errors, wrong values uniform); coh_ratio_shuf = the same with position-shuffled copies of the model's own error table; coh_ratio_depol = maxwrong / ((1 - lambda^2)/q) (the depolarizing value is a MEAN over inputs, so even i.i.d. fields exceed it at the max).

exponent_fully_correctable_models.definition: rate_min = worst-input exponent I_min = min_x -ln(1 - (sqrt T_x(0) - sqrt T_x(h*))^2); rate_law = the same for the depolarizing channel at the model's eps; votes needed scale as 1/rate.  Models with every input correctable only.

indicator_structure_eps_0p05_to_0p95.definition: z = (G - dof)/sqrt(2 dof), G = 2 N MI(error indicator; feature) in nats, dof = levels - 1; gz_coord_max = max over the input coordinates, gz_label = feature is the true label f(x). Under independence z is approximately standard normal (the max over n coordinates slightly more).

A3.definition: an input x is correctable iff T_x(0) > max_{h != 0} T_x(h) (exact integer comparison); frac_correctable is over ALL inputs of G (x = 0 is always correctable).  Per training run: eps_all = largest eps among its snapshots at which every input is correctable, eps_some = smallest eps among its snapshots at which some input is not.  Snapshots are discrete, so eps_all is a lower bound on the run's last fully-correctable error rate.

zero_vote_mechanism_all_models.definition: zero vote = M(x+r) = M(r), i.e. vote offset h = -f(x) (the corrector would output 0).  gmax_is_minus_f: the largest wrong-vote mass of the model sits at h = -f(x).  frac_hstar_minus_f: fraction of inputs (x != 0, f(x) != 0) whose strongest wrong value is -f(x) (chance 1/(q-1) for incoherent errors).  frac_unc_beaten_by_minus_f: among uncorrectable inputs with f(x) != 0, the fraction where the zero vote ties or beats the truth.  Two-histogram criterion: predict 'mostly correctable' iff err_collision (sum_v pi_v^2, the mean truth mass) exceeds out_collision (sum_c mu_c^2, the mean zero-vote mass); both are histograms, no channel needed.

A5.selection_rule: highest_eps_fully_correctable = the add/grok model with the largest eps among those whose every input is correctable; lowest_eps_with_uncorrectable = the add/grok model with the smallest eps among those with at least one uncorrectable input

outputs.definition: mu = histogram of the model's predicted class over all inputs, mu_err = over its wrong inputs only; collision = sum of squares (1/q if balanced).  The 'zero vote' is M(x+r) = M(r), offset h = -f(x); its mass averaged over x != 0 equals (|G| sum mu^2 - 1)/(|G| - 1) exactly.

hstar_linear_fit_top40.note: number of the 40 smallest-margin inputs x = (a, b) whose strongest wrong value equals alpha a + beta b mod p, maximised over all p^2 linear forms

highest_eps_fully_correctable.dependence_definition: nmi_indicator = MI(1[e != 0]; feature)/H(1[e != 0]); nmi_value = MI(e; feature)/H(e) with e the error value including 0; nulls from 200 random permutations of the positions; z = (observed - null mean)/null sd.  error_rate_by_level = error rate within each of the p level sets of the feature.

A4.selection_rule: add/grok p=47: for each target eps in (0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.65) the snapshot with the smallest |eps - target| among the runs with split_seed = init_seed = 0 (ties: lower train_frac, then earlier step); if no seed-0 snapshot lies within 0.03 of the target, the closest snapshot over all seeds.  lin: the same rule with target 0.3.  add/memo: the random-hold-out model with train_frac 0.7 (eps = 0.30), split_seed 0, init_seed 0.
A4.definition: exact_mean = mean over ALL inputs of G of the exact failure probability of the plurality of k votes (tie = failure) computed from the model's exact twirled channel; exact_worst = max over inputs.  pred_* = the same routine applied to the depolarizing channel at the model's eps (identical for every x != 0; the mean includes x = 0, which never fails).  chernoff_* = core.chernoff_union_bound.  Values below 1e-10 are at the accuracy floor of the exact routine (absolute accuracy ~1e-12) and are flagged; where the Chernoff bound of the worst input is already below 1e-11 the exact routine is skipped and only the bound is given.  real_* = actual votes with core.sc_fail (100 repetitions for every input; 20000 for the worst input); z = (empirical - exact)/SE.
